specification.title: Kassir
specification.description: A Tauri v2 desktop cashier application (Point of Sale) for Windows. Sells and restocks goods, records arbitrary transactions, and keeps products, stock, customers, suppliers, payment methods, contacts, pockets and analytics. Offline-first: one SQLite database (data.db) is the source of truth, fronted by an Effect services layer (src/services/) whose SubscriptionRefs components subscribe to, and read through the page-data layer (src/components/page-data/). Includes thermal receipt printing (pdf-lib + the Windows spooler), role-based access (admin/user), multi-cashier login, and a timestamp-based cloud sync protocol that is documented (backend-docs/openapi.yaml) but not implemented in the app — see <sync_system>.

design_system.description: shadcn/ui new-york style, zinc base, CSS variables, light and dark via next-themes. Typography is a four-token scale declared in global.css and re-resolved per app size: `text-big`, `text-normal`, `text-small`, and the owner-reserved `text-tiny`, plus `text-change` and `text-grand-total` for the cart's money. The UI size preference ("big" | "small") toggles a `small` class on <body>, and every `small:` variant hangs off it. `src/lib/design-tokens.test.ts` guards the rule mechanically: no raw `text-3xl`/`text-sm`, and no lucide `size={N}` (an attribute no `.small` rule can override) — icon size comes from `icon`/`size-*` classes so both modes stay correct. Every <DialogContent> must render a <DialogDescription> or say `aria-describedby={undefined}` on purpose; `src/lib/dialog-description.test.ts` guards it.

conventions.rule: A page never touches SQLite, plugin-store or localStorage. Every read and write goes through a service (src/services/<name>). A service writes the database first, then its SubscriptionRef, so subscribers see the write with no refresh call. Bounded catalogs are a full-list ref (products, methods, extras, customers, suppliers, socials, cashiers, pockets); unbounded ones (records, money entries) are queried Effects plus a `revision` counter that a query puts in its deps.

Async page data goes through createPageData (src/components/page-data/): one key per independent read, the read lives at the leaf that renders the value, fine-grained gates with value-sized placeholders (never a whole-card swap), reserved card heights, a 200 ms anti-flash window, and writes that name the keys they invalidate. See <frontend> / page_data and .pi/skills/page-data.md.

Money arithmetic is decimal.js everywhere — never float `+ - *` on rupiah. `src/lib/purchase` holds the cart math (line subtotal/grand total, discount stack, extras, paid total, transaction grand total, roundMoney); the record's own precision (`record_fix`) is applied by `~/services/record/round.ts` (roundToFix) and by `roundMoney`, so the table and the printed receipt cannot disagree by a rounding step.

Dates are Temporal (temporal-polyfill) in the shop's time zone (`tz` in lib/constants), never the browser's raw Date arithmetic. A record belongs to the day `COALESCE(record_paid_at, record_credit_at, record_created_at)` says — the same effective date the day list, Beranda and Analytics use.

Bitfields are documented in FLAGS.md and defined beside their service: records.record_flag (RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT = 1), tx_records.tx_record_flag (STORED_FLAG = 0b01, ADJUSTMENT_CART_FLAG = 0b10), products.product_flag (PRODUCT_FLAG_UNPUBLISHED = 0b1), and the extras flags (DUAL_FLAG = 0b1, carried from extras into tx_extras into record_extras). Never reuse a bit.

Anything listening on `window` consults isScreenOwnedByDialog() (src/hooks/use-dialog-lock) before acting: a cart money editor is a `modal={false}` Radix dialog portaled beside #root, so `inert` and the focus trap do not stop a window keydown. useInertApp(open) registers the lock and makes #root inert/aria-hidden while the editor is open.
A page must not import another page's hook or helper. Shared behaviour is lifted to src/hooks or src/components, and shared page data to a service.

Services fail with a Data.TaggedError per domain (ProductError, RecordError, …). Pages either catch the typed failure (createErrorBoundary / pageData.Gate error prop) or render the sentence; the driver's text never reaches the screen (DbError splits `message` from `detail`).

entry_point.file: Windows entry point (#[windows_subsystem = "windows"] in release); calls kassir_lib::run().
Plugin registration (single-instance, dialog, fs, log, store, sql with migrations, prevent-default, optional mcp-bridge), the five-command invoke handler, and the app run loop.
generate_migration(): embeds every `src-tauri/src/database/<range>/migration-N.sql` as a tauri-plugin-sql Migration for `sqlite:data.db`.

command.name: hash_password
command.description: bcrypt at DEFAULT_COST on the blocking pool (~250 ms of CPU; running it inline would stall the command runtime). Returns the hash.

command.name: verify_password
command.signature: async fn(password: String, hash: String) → Result<bool, AuthError>
command.description: Verifies a plaintext password against a stored bcrypt hash, also on the blocking pool.

command.name: get_printers
command.description: Enumerates Windows printers via winprint. The error lists the available printers when a lookup fails.

command.name: print_pdf
command.signature: fn(printer_name: String, pdf_bytes: Vec<u8>) → Result<String, String>
command.description: Validates the %PDF header, writes the bytes to a named temp file, prints through WinPdfPrinter, removes the file, and returns the cashier-facing sentence ("Dikirim ke printer …") the test-print screen shows.

command.name: export_file
command.signature: async fn(default_name: String, contents: String) → Result<Option<String>, String>
command.description: The JSON download. The Save dialog and the write both live in Rust: the fs plugin's scope is narrowed to the app's own image and log directories, so a frontend writeFile on a user-picked path is rejected. Returns the written path, or None when the dialog was cancelled.

security.description: No embedded HTTP server, no JWT, no sync token in the app binary: the cloud sync protocol lives only in backend-docs/openapi.yaml. Passwords hash and verify through the two bcrypt commands above; the session is frontend state (the auth service), persisted in localStorage.
security.single_instance: tauri-plugin-single-instance is registered first, before any window or database work. The model is one process per machine: data.db is preloaded and the catalogue/cart live in process-local refs, so a second launch would debounce-write its own stale snapshot over the first. A second launch focuses the existing window instead.

capabilities.description: Mirrors src-tauri/capabilities/*.json, which src/lib/tauri-capability.test.ts guards: least privilege, no filesystem default, no updater, no process control. A permission nothing calls is a permission that must not be granted.

capability.name: default
capability.permission: core:window:allow-destroy → useFlushOnExit closes the window itself; once a JS listener sits on tauri://close-requested, Rust prevent_close()s, and core:window:default does not include destroy
sql:default, sql:allow-execute → the whole SQLite layer (src/services/db)

capability.name: mcp-bridge
capability.permission: mcp-bridge:default → 127.0.0.1:9223 automation bridge, enabled only by tauri.dev.conf.json and the `mcp-bridge` Cargo feature

database.name: data.db
database.description: The only database. Every migration in src-tauri/src/database/<range>/migration-N.sql is embedded by database/mod.rs and applied on boot; the frontend also applies the same files in the e2e harness. The schema evolved from INTEGER keys to TEXT (ULID) keys with `_updated_at` / `_sync_at` bookkeeping. Key steps: - 1-10: initial tables (products, records, record_items), discounts, rounding, credit, capital - 11-20: barcode to TEXT, capital fixes, cashiers with a password hash, record redesign - 21-30: price/capital to REAL, images, socials, money, payment methods - 31-40: TEXT (ULID) keys, product_events (event-sourced stock), sync columns; money-kind renamed to pocket - 41: pocket ordering (money_kind_ordering, carried onto pockets later) - 42: extras.extra_flag - 43: the schema rewrite — products split into listings / properties / images / stocks, records into record_listings / record_methods / record_extras / record_images / discounts, every syncable row gains a `<singular>_deleted_at` soft-delete column (graves/graves_kind retired), and the tx_* cart tables are ported into data.db (tx.db is no longer preloaded). Replaced tables are parked as `<name>_old`; nothing was dropped - 44: the backfill — every old row copied into the new shape, parent-first, no DDL - 45: a no-op bridge slot, so databases that recorded a 46 from another branch still line up - 46: adds image/webp to img_mimes Read indexes for the hot queries (records' effective date, listings, product_events' product/stock/record) are created in 43.

entry.file: Creates the ReactDOM root on #root, renders RouterProvider with the hash router, imports global.css. No StrictMode.
SPA entry, lang="id", body class "overflow-y-hidden", #root as a flex column.

routing.description: Hash router (createHashRouter) in src/route.tsx. Pages are imported eagerly except three deliberate lazy boundaries: the Home page body (the heaviest dashboard), Analytics' five bodies (recharts + d3), and the product Performance tab. The receipt's pdf-lib is loaded lazily by the shared print program (src/pages/Setting/Printer/util-program-print.ts, `import("~/lib/receipt")`), not by the router. The Dev/PageData and Dev/PageCache playgrounds only exist when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true.

guards.description: There is no route middleware. Protection is the AuthLayout component plus in-page role checks, and the shortcuts are not role-gated, so the in-page check is what actually stops a non-admin.
guards.guard: Subscribes to service.auth.changes; while the session resolves it renders a loader, on null it redirects to /login. Wraps every route but /login.
Children for admins, `<Redirect to={fallback}>` for everyone else. Used by Setting shop/data/log and Extra new.
Renders `<Redirect to="/">` itself when useUser().role is not admin.
Admins get the edit form; other roles get a read-only info panel.
guards.note: Setting printer is reachable by any signed-in user: the sidebar hides it from non-admins but the route is ungated (see <open_questions>).

layouts.layout: Subscribes to service.config.size.changes and toggles the `small` class on <body> before paint (layout effect), which drives every Tailwind `small:` variant.

The session guard, the sticky Topbar, the main-body scrollport, the Outlet, the sonner Toaster, the alt+N shortcuts and the close-flush handler. The shell is h-dvh with #main-body as `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto`: pages get a definite height from this chain, which is what every `h-full` page and its scroll box relies on — do not go back to min-height on the shell. Back button (unless on "/"), the route title (longest-prefix map), the dynamic shop title, TopNavList, Refresh and SettingLink. Desktop tab bar: Toko (/pos), Restock (/restock), Produk (/products), Riwayat (/records), Uang (/money, admin only). The shop name from the info service, shown once the form has answered. window.location.reload(); there is no cache to bust. Gear → /setting, with the alt+5 hint. alt+0..5 navigation, alt legend toggle, dialog-lock and editable-target guards. On window close, flushes the cart service and destroys the window; `core:window:allow-destroy` exists for it. @xstate/store atom for the 5-second Kbd legend.

group.name: navigation
group.description: Registered by useNavigationShortcuts in the authenticated layout. Holding Alt toggles the Kbd legend (5 s). Suppressed inside inputs/textarea/select/contenteditable, for AltGr, and whenever a dialog owns the screen.

group.name: cart
group.description: The Pos and Restock screens share these through useCartScreen / the cart components. All are ignored while a dialog owns the screen or a commit is in flight.

shortcut.action: Put the cursor in the goods search (Restock first leaves the payment stage)
Go to the payment rows (Restock opens its payment stage); settle the sale once the tender is ready
Previous / next open cart tab, skipping parked carts; editors keep their word-jump
In the payment strip: swap the row's method kind (cash, qris, transfer, debit)
Copy the selected goods cell / paste into it (value, not display text; the paste stays in select mode)
Undo the cell editor's last change

error_boundary.description: Route-level ErrorBoundary: Unauthenticated → hard redirect to /login; route error responses (404/403) with contextual icons; anything else with the stack in DEV only. Feature-level boundaries come from createErrorBoundary/createManyErrorBoundary (typed, rethrowing foreign errors), and the page-data layer renders an inline error per key instead of throwing.

auth_module.description: src/lib/auth.ts is only the two Tauri bridges — hash(password) and verify(password, storedHash) — plus the Unauthenticated error. The session lives in the auth service: persisted under the localStorage key "user" through the hidden local-storage service, validated with a Zod schema { id, name, role }, and checked against the cashiers table on hydrate (a session pointing at a deleted cashier is dropped and the key cleared). auth.get / auth.set / auth.changes drive the guard, useUser() and the topbar.

page_data.description: src/components/page-data/ — the async-data convention every page follows. createPageData<Data, Error>(name, { cache }) returns a typed namespace: `Provider` registers the page's sources (a Stream per key, keyed by name) and starts them together; `Gate` renders a set of keys with a pulse placeholder, an error slot, a delay (200 ms anti-flash by default) and a render prop that receives exactly the gated values; `use(key)` reads one key without gating; `useFrame(keys)` returns the status and first error for a static frame that must survive a failure; `useStatus` / `useRefresh` / `useMutate` cover the rest. The cache (z-cache.ts, exported as `pageCache`) keeps the last answer per tag+deps in memory, paints it on a return visit, and invalidates on a write or a revision bump; `Dev/PageCache` is its inspector.
page_data.component: keys, pulse, error (node or typed render prop), delay, children({...values}). The old Result-based Gate survives only in Dev/PageData, which demonstrates the difference.
Holds the region's space from the first frame but stays invisible for the anti-flash window (useDelayedFlag). For regions whose shape the skeleton authors (forms, a total's box).
The real control, disabled and empty, with only its text pulsing — the box, border, padding and chevron never move.
statusOf / statusOfGroup: pending | ready | refreshing | failed | stale, with `stale` deliberately not `failed` (a working value from a failed refresh).
page_data.rule: Two reads that fail independently get two keys. A value that needs two reads declares both; a value that needs one declares one, so it can land first.
A card's floor is a min-height (ROWS_FLOOR), never a measurement, so the skeleton and the real content occupy the same box.
A page does not block on one top-level Loader: chrome is on the first frame, values fill in (or pulse) inside it.

cart.description: The POS machinery in src/components/cart/, shared by Pos (sale), Restock (purchase) and, for its tab model, /transaction. A cart is a `tx_records` row plus tx_listings / tx_discounts / tx_extras / tx_methods / tx_images, owned by the transaction service; every edit is written through, so a refresh reopens the same cart. The open cart and the stage are URL values (`?draft=`, `?stage=`), and tab switches replace history.
cart.component: The draft lifecycle: always have a cart, start one on demand, open/close/store/restore tabs, the tab walker (Ctrl+Arrow), F1/F2/F12, the dialog lock, and the stage reset on tab switch.
The one Bayar: refuses when not ready, blurs the active cell, marks the screen busy, calls transaction.submit exactly once, then toasts the failure or hands the payload to the completion dialog.
The goods grid — one line per row, editable cells (name/code/unit/price/qty/discount), per-cell issues, the search panel, scan-to-add, clipboard, undo.
The payment strip: one row per method of a kind, split payments, Ctrl+0..3 kind swap, the money editors as `modal={false}` dialogs with useInertApp.
The charge grid: preset catalog search, percent/number kinds, the dual-flag charge carried into the record.
The keyboard model: columns, rows, selection, editing, and the per-column constraints, kept pure so the grids cannot drift apart.
Kind vs method: a kind offers its named accounts then its base method; freeMethodId/nextFreeKind/kindExhausted enforce one method per transaction.
The duplicate/unregistered-code checks that block Bayar, with links to the products involved.
The completion dialog's tender rows: zero rows dropped, base methods labelled from their kind, a deleted method keeps its money.
CartBody (the completion dialog's stable slot) and CartPanels (the `inert` panel column with the blocking overlay while submitting).

component.name: z-Complete / z-PaymentTime / z-Note / z-Precision / z-Total / z-StartError / z-Issue

cart.component: The completion dialog (print receipt, undo), the paid-at picker, the draft note, the money precision select, the grand total, the could-not-start-cart panel and the inline issue renderers.

shared_components.component: Subscribes a hot Stream (a service's changes) to React state and returns a Result; interrupts the fiber on unmount.
useStream plus a factory and deps, re-subscribing when they change. keepPrevious holds the last value while a refetch is in flight and flags it `refetching`.
Runs an Effect on demand and tracks pending/error/data; mutate resolves with an Either so callers branch without try/catch.
Renders a Result: init → fallback (delayed 200 ms so fast loads do not flash), error → throws to the nearest boundary, success → children. LoaderMany does the same for several results.
Builds a React error boundary for one or more typed error classes; foreign errors rethrow to an ancestor boundary. createManyErrorBoundary takes several.
Role guard / hash-router-aware redirect (optional hard reload).
Conditional render (by `when`, or by `value` where only null/undefined fall through) and the keyed array map.

The locale-aware numeric input (caret survives grouping dots), the password field with reveal, the import file panel (keyboard-reachable, drop or click), and the payment-method picker (kind + account).
The date picker, the URL-driven range picker, and the Temporal-backed date+time field (a DateTimeField, never a native datetime-local).

component.name: Loading / Spinner / TextError / ErrorComponent / NotFound / SaveError

shared_components.component: The small states: centered spinner, inline spinner, one-line error, full-page error, 404 panel, and the cart's failed-save banner (toasted once, cleared by a later success).

ui_primitives.description: shadcn/ui primitives on Radix in src/components/ui/. new-york, zinc, CSS variables, lucide.
ui_primitives.component: Text controls plus the Field/FieldLabel/FieldError wrapper.
Rupiah input: grouped `Rp`, comma decimals, caret by digit, optional sign.
Percent input: `%` suffix, comma decimals, clamped to [min, max].

component.name: checkbox / radio-group / select / combobox / slider / switch / tabs / accordion / popover / dialog / separator

ui_primitives.component: Radix primitives, plus a custom Combobox (Popover + Input over a filtered list, search debounced by SEARCH_DELAY). Dialog requires a description or an explicit `aria-describedby={undefined}`.
Table parts, Skeleton + SkeletonText, Kbd/KbdGroup, and the sonner Toaster.

testing.description: Three layers, plus mechanical guards. Unit tests sit beside the code as *.test.ts(x) and are run by `bun test` (happy-dom preloaded, @testing-library matchers, afterEach cleanup). Integration tests live in src/integration/ and wire the real service layers over the real migrations with only the Tauri backends substituted (db/store/local-storage test-support). End-to-end specs live in e2e/ and drive /e2e.html, whose in-browser harness (src/e2e/) runs the same migration files on sql.js and injects the service before the router is imported.
testing.layer: *.test.ts(x) beside the module; service tests use makeTestDatabase (bun:sqlite + every migration) and the Map-backed store/local-storage fakes; page/data hook tests use a real MemoryRouter; Tauri commands are stubbed with mock.module at the module boundary.

src/integration/: the real service layers over the real migrations, the real page-data layer and the real page components — only the Tauri backends are substituted. home.test.tsx (Beranda's keys over the record/money services), product-page.test.tsx (catalogue reads and write-through), shop-settings.test.tsx (Setting → Toko's form writing to the store), and the till pair pos.test.tsx + restock.test.tsx. The till pair drives the cart screens the way the operator does: scan into the grid (type + Enter before the debounce), bump a quantity, edit the inline tender, walk Restock's stages, open the completion dialog, park a tab, press F12 / Ctrl+Arrow / F2. What it pins is the joins — a scan becomes a line and a total, Bayar gates on the tender, a commit writes the record and moves stock the right way, a credit purchase books a debt, a dual charge commits its extras-only twin, Batalkan rewinds a sale into a draft. `till-harness.tsx` builds a fresh database, store, session and service per test and offers the common helpers; `service-proxy.ts` is the injection seam.
testing.rule: Integration tests hand the pages a service through `src/integration/service-proxy.ts` (a stable proxy over `globalThis.__KASSIR_SERVICE__`, set per test) instead of `mock.module("~/services")`: bun caches a module across test files, so a second file's mock never takes effect and the pages keep the first file's service.
testing.layer: e2e/*.e2e.ts via Playwright against /e2e.html: seeded SQL/storage, a real login, then assertions on the actual screens (pos-cart, transaction, analytics, publish, page-data, page-cache, …).

guards.guard: No raw text sizes, no lucide size={N}; the four text tokens are the hierarchy.
Every DialogContent has a DialogDescription or an explicit aria-describedby={undefined}.
The shipped capability stays least-privilege (no fs:default, no updater, no process).
The version constant matches package.json (a release that forgets one bump site fails).

connection.description: One database, data.db, preloaded by @tauri-apps/plugin-sql and migrated on boot by the embedded Rust migration list. The only frontend accessor is the hidden `db` service (src/services/db/) — domain services never touch plugin-sql themselves. DatabaseService exposes execute, selectMany, selectOne and transaction, each wrapped in Effect with a DbError. `transaction` joins its statements into one execute call: plugin-sql has no transaction handle, but a single execute is atomic, so a cross-table write is one multi-statement string with renumbered placeholders. Raw SQL, parameterized; no ORM.
connection.file: DatabaseService interface, Binding/Statement types, DbError { message, detail }.
DatabaseLive — a lazily loaded handle behind Layer.succeed.

schema.description: The authoritative schema is the migration set in src-tauri/src/database/. Since migration 43 the aggregates are decomposed (products → listings/properties/images/stocks; records → record_listings/record_methods/ record_extras/record_images/discounts), syncable rows carry `_updated_at` / `_sync_at` / `_deleted_at`, and the `tx_*` cart tables live in the same file. `stocks` is a local cache rebuilt from the append-only `product_events` journal. Tables replaced by 43 are parked as `<name>_old` and are never read; nothing was dropped, so they remain on disk.

group.name: catalog
group.table: product_id, product_name, product_note, product_flag (bit 0 = unpublished), sync trio
one priced unit of a product; listing_name/price/unit/kind/code (code unique across live listings, NOCASE), soft delete
the local lot cache: stock_value, stock_capital, created/updated; never synced
append-only stock journal (manual/inc/dec), linked to the record and the stock lot; indexed by product, stock and record
alternative names, key/value properties, image references (name + mime under AppData/images); img_mimes is the allowed set (png/jpeg/webp)

group.name: history
group.table: header: created/paid/credit dates, mode (incoming|outcoming), flag, totals, customer/supplier snapshots, sync trio, deleted_at
the line's snapshot: name, code, unit, price, qty, capital, total, product/listing link, portions
one row per payment applied (split payments); record_pay mirrors the sum
charges/deductions snapshotted with their flag (DUAL_FLAG books the twin record)
pictures attached to a record
one row per discount on a record line, with eff (the rupiah it took)

group.name: cart
group.description: The tx_* tables are working state, deleted when a cart commits. See <database> / cart_tables.
group.table: a tab: title, mode, flag (parked bit / adjustment bit), note, fix, rounding, customer/supplier text, paid_at, order
the goods lines, with the catalogue values snapshotted (name, code, unit, price, qty, base)
per-line discounts, whole-cart charges, payments, attached images

group.name: directories
group.table: login accounts (name UNIQUE, role, bcrypt hash); not synced
sale-side and purchase-side counterparties, name-sorted, soft delete
the payment catalog: base rows (name NULL) + named accounts, kind cash|qris|transfer|debit
the charge catalog with extra_flag (DUAL_FLAG)
receipt contact lines
the cash journal: pocket types absolute|change, entries with timestamp/value/note, soft delete

table.name: mode_enum / value_kind_enum / product_event_enum / money_type / role_enum / versions

group.table: lookup tables and the migration bookkeeping

ownership.description: Which table — or store/localStorage key — each service is the only writer of.
ownership.owner: products, listings, properties, images, stocks, product_events, product_names
records, record_listings, record_methods, record_extras, record_images, discounts
tx_records, tx_listings, tx_discounts, tx_extras, tx_methods, tx_images
store keys: name, owner, address, header, footer, show-cashier

caching.description: A service's SubscriptionRef is the cache: reads come from the ref once hydrated; a write goes to SQLite first and then updates the ref, so subscribers see it with no explicit refresh. Queried domains (records, money entries, analytics) expose a `revision` counter instead, which a query puts in its deps. The one sanctioned revalidate is product.refresh()/refreshMany(), because a record or transaction write moves stock behind the product aggregate's back. On top of that, page-data's pageCache keeps the last answer per tag+deps in memory and invalidates on writes/revisions; it never touches disk.

cart_tables.description: The tab-based cart, ported into data.db by migration 43 (tx.db is no longer preloaded). Not synced. A tab is a `tx_records` row; its goods are `tx_listings`, its charges `tx_extras`, its payments `tx_methods`, its line discounts `tx_discounts` (hanging off a listing), its pictures `tx_images`. Committing writes the record and deletes the tab in one transaction; `transaction.add.fromRecord` rebuilds a tab from a saved record, and `record.delete` on a record it came from never leaves a stale tab behind.

record_commit.description: Three writers, all in the record service, all one multi-statement transaction: `record.add.draft` (a live cart: header, lines, discounts, extras, payments, stock movement, tx_* delete), `record.add.external` (an imported record, under a new id) and `record.add.adjustment` (a hand-typed extras-only record, flagged RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT). A sale drains `stocks` oldest-first (a purchase receives a new cost lot) through the pure builders in product/stock-sql.ts. A purchase's capital: its per-pc cost is the grand total split by each line's own total, then rounded to the record's `record_fix` before it reaches `stocks.stock_capital` and `record_listings.record_listing_capital` — the same precision lot matching and the Modal column compare with. When a draft's DUAL_FLAG extras are present, `add.draft` also writes the extras-only `outcoming` twin in the same commit, both rows stamped with each other's id in `record_pair_id`. A line that points at a catalogue listing is also the operator's latest word on the goods (record/sql/catalogue.ts): its edited name is written back to listings.listing_name — and to products.product_name when that product has a single live listing — while its price is written back only on a sale and only in the listing's own unit. Codes and units are never written back; the record keeps its own snapshot either way.

services.description: Domain state lives in Effect services at src/services/<name>/ — index.ts is the interface only, live.ts is the Layer. Each owns a SubscriptionRef as its single source of truth and exposes reads as Effects plus a changes Stream; a write goes to SQLite first and then the ref. Components subscribe with useStream/useQuery or, preferably, through page-data. Typed errors are caught by createErrorBoundary or rendered per key by pageData.Gate. src/services/index.ts composes the layers and exports the app-level `service` object. Public services: analytics, auth, cashier, config, customer, extra, info, listing, log, method, money, printer, product, record, social, supplier, transaction. Hidden backends: db, store, local-storage.

hidden_backends.backend: execute / selectMany / selectOne / transaction over data.db; DbError { message, detail }. See <database>.
plugin-store key-value: get / set / remove; StoreError, NotFound.
localStorage key-value: get / set / remove; LocalStorageError, NotFound.

service.name: analytics
service.description: Read-only aggregates over saved records for /analytics. Shared rules: deleted records out, record_flag bit 0 (hand-typed adjustments) out, and a record counted on its effective date COALESCE(paid_at, credit_at, created_at).

interface.method: Per local day, per direction, with the unpaid part of the day.
Per day, from lines that stored a cost; `costed` says whether a margin means anything.
Sales per local hour, and per ISO weekday (1 = Monday).
Every product that moved, with qty, revenue, margin, costed lines.
The lines behind one group, newest first.
What was actually tendered, grouped by method kind.

service.name: auth
service.description: The signed-in session, persisted under the localStorage key "user".
service.state: One SubscriptionRef holding User | null. Hydrating validates the stored id against the cashiers table; a session pointing at a deleted cashier is dropped and the key cleared.

interface.method: User | null.
Persist (or clear) the session; null signs out.
Stream<User | null>. Drives the AuthLayout guard, useUser() and the topbar.

service.name: cashier
service.description: Login accounts. Local-only — cashiers are not synced. Names are stored trimmed with inner whitespace collapsed, and cashier_name is UNIQUE, so a duplicate is refused as a CashierError rather than a driver string.

interface.method: The roster, name-sorted. byId also returns the bcrypt hash and fails with NotFound.
Create an account; the caller hashes the password.
Rename, re-role, or replace the stored hash.
Remove the account (a real delete; cashiers are not synced).

service.note: Hashing and verification live in lib/auth (Tauri bcrypt commands); the service stores whatever hash it is handed.

service.name: config
service.description: The UI preferences: size, and the product list's layout. Owns the localStorage keys "size" and "product-view".

interface.method: Current size: "big" | "small".
Persist, then push to subscribers.
Stream<Size>. RootLayout turns it into the body class; useSize() reads it.
Current product layout: "grid" | "table"; anything else stored reads as "grid".
Set in memory, then persist. A failed write reports ConfigError but keeps the session on the chosen view.

service.note: The product list keeps its view in the URL while it is open; productView is only the seed a bare `/products` reads. Unlike `size` there is no `changes` stream — no one subscribes, the URL is the live value.

service.name: customer
service.description: Sale-side customers (name, phone), read by the cart, the record pages and the Customer screen.

interface.method: Name-sorted; unsync is the rows the sync layer has not pushed.
Clears customer_sync_at so the change is pushed.
Soft delete via customer_deleted_at.

service.name: extra
service.description: The surcharge/discount catalog. The DUAL_FLAG bit in `flag` marks an extra that books twice: a sale carrying it also commits an extras-only `outcoming` record for the same money (see record.add.draft and records.record_pair_id). The flag is copied into the cart (tx_extra_flag) and the record (record_extra_flag), because the cart has no id link to the catalog. ValueKind (number | percent) lives in lib/constants and is shared with records.

interface.method: Ordered by name in SQL; a write re-reads the row and re-sorts locally.
Soft delete via extra_deleted_at.

service.name: info
service.description: The shop identity on receipts and in the title bar: name, owner, address, header, footer, showCashier.

interface.method: Writes all six store keys together; a partial change reads first and patches (Setting/Shop/util-patch-info), so the form and the cashier checkbox cannot blank each other.
Stream<Info>. Feeds the receipt, the title and the Setting shop form.

service.name: listing
service.description: The sellable catalogue the POS and Restock grids read: one row per listing (not per product), with its cover image, the parent's name and alternative names, and the parent's total stock. Derived from `product`, so it has no state of its own.

interface.method: Every published listing.
Name/code match over src/lib/search/listings (fuzzy ladder + signature-cached index). A blank query returns nothing.
Stream<LogPage>: the tail (last LOG_VIEW_LIMIT lines, newest first, warnings included) plus the file's real line count. Every subscription re-reads the file.
Empty the file; subscribers re-read it.

service.name: method
service.description: Payment methods and the per-kind default. The catalog lives in SQLite (four base rows with name NULL plus named accounts; methods.method_name is ordered NULLS-first inside a kind) and the defaults live in store.json, one key per defaultable kind ("default-transfer" | "default-debit" | "default-qris"). One ref holds both slices so a reader sees the catalog and the defaults together; a rename or delete re-reads only the method slice, and a default change keeps the method array's identity.

interface.method: null clears the kind's default.
Soft delete; record_methods rows keep their method.

service.name: money
service.description: Money pockets and their ledger. Owns the `pockets` and `money` tables (pocket_* columns). Reads filter *_deleted_at IS NULL; deletes are soft, and deleting a pocket soft-deletes its entries too (the FK cascade only fires on a physical delete). A pocket is `absolute` (each entry is the balance as typed) or `change` (the page adds each entry's delta to the balance the ledger last held).
service.state: One SubscriptionRef of PocketSummary[] — each pocket joined to its most recent entry (timestamp DESC, money_id DESC for ties) — so a reorder, rename or new entry reaches subscribers. Entry lists are queried, driven by entries.get.revision.

group.name: pockets
group.method: Soft-delete the pocket and every entry it holds.

group.name: entries
group.method: Insert unless the pocket already holds an entry at that instant (DuplicateError).

service.name: printer
service.description: The receipt printer: the system printer name plus the paper width in mm. Owns the store keys printer_name and printer_width; a width that is not a positive number falls back to 80.

interface.method: Read by the Setting printer page and the receipt print path.

service.name: product
service.description: The product aggregate: a product with its listings (priced units, at most one code each, unique across live listings), properties, alternative names, images and stock lots. The read model's `stock` and `capital` are derived — the sum of the lots and their weighted-average cost. Owns products, listings, properties, product_names, images, stocks and product_events.
service.error: Plus ProductDuplicateCode, carrying the code that was already taken.
service.state: One SubscriptionRef of the whole read model; a write re-hydrates the touched rows, and get.changes / changesFull / unsync read from it.

method.name: get.all / get.byId / get.byCode / get.unsync / get.performance(id, range) / get.changes / get.changesFull

interface.method: One transaction: the product, at least one listing, optional codes, and one stock lot. Values are validated here (no negative price or cost basis from any writer).

method.name: set.info / set.publish(id, published) / set.listing.{add, update, remove} / set.property.{add, update, remove} / set.productName.{add, update, remove} / set.image.{add, commit, remove, reorder}

interface.method: FIFO consume and cost-lot receive; the pure builders in product/stock-sql.ts are shared with the record service.
Soft-delete the product; children ride the aggregate.
Re-hydrate after a record or transaction write moves stock — the one sanctioned revalidate.

service.name: record
service.description: Committed transactions and everything snapshotted with them: listing lines with their discounts, extras, split payments and images. Owns records, record_listings, record_methods, record_extras, record_images and discounts. The mode follows the money, not the goods: `incoming` is a sale (money in, stock consumed), `outcoming` a purchase (money out, stock received).
service.state: Records are a queried domain (always read by range), so there is no full-list ref: reads are Effects and get.revision is a counter bumped on every write, which a queried page puts in its deps.

interface.method: Records whose effective date falls in [start, end), newest first, optionally narrowed by a listing-name match done in SQL.
The full record: lines (regrouped from portions), discounts, extras, methods, images.
Capped page of matching lines plus the total match count; a blank query returns nothing.
Unsettled credit records, newest first.
Write counter a queried page re-reads on.
Per-mode count and sum for a range.
A hand-typed extras-only record (RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT); no stock moves.
Import a record made elsewhere under a new id, moving stock by the same rules as a live record.

Commit a live cart: header, lines, discounts, extras, payments, stock movement and the tx_* delete, in one transaction; with `mirror`, the DUAL_FLAG twin is written in the same commit. See <database> / record_commit.

method.name: set.paidAt / set.creditAt / set.note / set.mode / set.payment / set.toCredit / set.payCredit

interface.note: set.mode does not rewrite the record in place: it soft-deletes the original, re-points every child at a copy and flips the stock journal, returning the new id — the page follows it instead of sitting on a tombstone.

set.payment rewrites every record_methods row from the submitted list (re-file a method, restate an amount, add or trim a split) and re-caches record_pay; the totals never move. The sum must cover the grand total (an underpayment is a credit), and an outstanding credit refuses it — its money arrives with set.payCredit. set.mode flips sale ↔ purchase and revisits the stock rules, striking the old movement from the journal first.
interface.method: Soft-delete and reverse the stock movement. A paired record takes its twin with it, so voiding a sale never leaves the extras-only outcoming half behind.

service.name: social
service.description: Receipt contact lines (name, value). Ordered by id so an edit does not reshuffle the printed receipt.

interface.method: Soft delete.

service.name: supplier
service.description: Purchase-side suppliers (name, note), read by the Restock cart. Mirrors the customer service.

method.name: add(name, note) => id / set.info(id, {name, note}) / delete.byId(id)

interface.method: Soft delete.

service.name: transaction
service.description: The open carts in tx_* tables, and the one place a cart becomes history. Owns tx_records, tx_listings, tx_discounts, tx_extras, tx_methods and tx_images. Every edit is written through (debounced), so a refresh reopens the same cart; a failed write surfaces through get.saveError rather than disappearing. Commit goes through record.add.draft; the adjustment screen commits through record.add.adjustment.
service.error: Plus SubmitError, a refusal the cashier can act on, whose `kind` lets the page route it (empty | stored | payment | name | code | price | outcoming).

interface.method: The open carts, oldest order first.
Stream<string | null>: null while every edit is on disk, a sentence once a write failed.
Write pending edits now; put a failure on the same channel.
Commit the cart and delete it; returns the record id.
Write the record back as a draft, then delete the record (reversing its stock movement).

method.name: set.{title, mode, fix, note, customer, customerName, customerPhone, supplier, supplierName, paidAt, rounding, store, restore}

interface.method: Saves the file under AppData/images and records the reference.
Hard delete — a cart is working state, not synced history.

cloud_api.description: The server contract lives in backend-docs/openapi.yaml. The app ships no HTTP client: no VITE_API_URL is read, no plugin-http is installed, and no src/server or src/lib/sync module exists. The protocol is timestamp-based and bidirectional: pull (GET /{entity}/{timestamp}) fetches rows updated after the cursor, push (POST /{entity}) uploads unsynced rows and returns { timestamp, failed[] }, and deletes are soft rows (see <sync_system>). Auth is one of three schemes, never mixed: cookieAdmin, cookieUser, or bearerApp for desktop/mobile sync.

entity.name: product
entity.endpoint: Push local products; failed ids come back.

entity.name: product-event
entity.endpoint: Events for the given product ids.

entity.name: record
entity.endpoint: Records updated after the cursor, with their lines, discounts, extras and payments.

sync_system.description: There is no sync implementation in the repository: src/lib/sync/, src/server/, src/lib/reqwest.ts and the Setting → Sync page are all gone, and nothing in the UI triggers a sync. What survives is the intended protocol (documented in backend-docs/openapi.yaml) and the schema that must be honoured when it is rebuilt: migration 43 replaced the graves tombstone exchange with a soft `<singular>_deleted_at` timestamp on every syncable row (customers, suppliers, socials, pockets, money, products, listings, properties, images, extras, methods, records), which syncs like any other update; products and records are now nested payloads (listings/stocks, record_listings/record_extras/record_methods/discounts); `stocks` is local-only and never pushed (product_events is the journal); cashiers are not synced. /api/grave is dead and should be dropped.

shape.stage: Read the entity's last-pull cursor (a store key), fetch count + rows, and merge into the local tables.
Insert a row the server has and draw has none; update when the server's updatedAt is newer than the local `_updated_at`; a soft-deleted row merges like any other update.
Read the entity's `unsync` set from its service, POST it, and mark the accepted ids synced (clear `_sync_at`).

sync_system.order: products → product_events → methods → records (records reference products and methods; events reference products).

requirements.item: Every merge/push has to go through the owning service (or a new sync service), not SQL from a page — the services own the refs the UI reads.
Deletion is a `_deleted_at` timestamp, not a tombstone table; the server must speak the same contract.
Last-writer-wins on `_updated_at`, with the server's timestamp as the tiebreak.
One "Sinkronisasi" action with per-entity pull/push progress, plus a resync that resets the cursors, and the floating status pill designed in <sync_ui_design>.

sync_ui_design.description: The intended UI for the rebuild, kept as a design record only: one Sinkronisasi button running the entities in order, per-entity rows that reveal as each starts, an Unduh (pull+merge) phase then an Unggah (push) phase, determinate pull bars from the /count endpoints (indeterminate for methods, which have no count endpoint), short-circuit on the first failure, and a compact ✓/✗ summary at the end. Sinkronisasi Ulang resets all cursors, marks everything unsynced, and runs the same flow. The button is disabled while a sync runs, and leaving the screen cancels the fiber, leaving the cursors untouched so the next run re-pulls.

pages.description: Every page below is routed and runs on the services layer. The two Dev/ pages exist only in a DEV build. Page behaviour is described from the code, not from an older plan.

page.name: login
page.description: Two-mode login over the cashier service. With no cashiers it shows FreshForm (Buat Toko: shop name, owner name, password), otherwise LoginForm (pick a cashier, enter the password). Already-signed-in users are redirected by AuthLayout.
page.fresh_form: Buat Toko: name, password, confirm. Creates the first admin (Rust hash_password → cashier.add), signs the session in through auth.set, and lands on /setting so the shop identity can be filled in next. It does not write the shop name itself.
page.login_form: Lists cashier names, verifies with the Rust verify_password command, then auth.set.

page.name: home
page.description: Beranda: a workspace, not a launcher. Header (shop name, day), three zero-blocking stat cards (masuk, keluar, utang) that each gate only the value they need, the day's ledger (six rows, reserved height, newest first), and — admins only — the pocket card. The menu grid of destinations sits underneath. Data comes from one provider with one key per question (today, yesterday, records, debt, pockets), each driven by the record revision so a commit reaches the page while it is open. Role is part of the provider deps, and the pockets key is left unsubscribed for cashiers.

page.name: pos
page.description: The sale screen. Two panels: the top walks the goods then the charges (two stages), the bottom carries the split payment rows, the change and the grand total. The cart and the stage live in the URL (`?draft=`, `?stage=`); F1/F2/F12, Ctrl+←/→ and Ctrl+0..3 are the operator's path. Nothing waits as a block: drafts, methods, customers and extras are registered on one page-data provider and start together. Bayar is the shared useSubmitCart flow (mode incoming): submit → transaction.add.draft, then the completion dialog with print and undo. See <cart>.

page.name: restock
page.description: The purchase screen — Pos's shape buying instead of selling. Three stages (goods, charges, payment) because a purchase settles through the stage panel; drafts, methods and suppliers load together. F2 opens the payment stage and puts the cursor on its first amount. A credit purchase is a settled flag on the same submit (useSubmitCart with credit), and the completion dialog prints the tender it took. Same shared cart machinery as Pos.

page.name: transaction
page.description: `/transaction` — an arbitrary record, typed by hand: no catalog, no search, no stages, no precision, no customer. Each tab is a real tx_records row flagged ADJUSTMENT_CART_FLAG; its lines are number extras, its direction, note and one payment live beside them. Committing calls record.add.adjustment (a records row flagged RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT, extras only, no stock) and deletes the tab. The tab is the source of truth: every edit goes through the service and the screen renders the stream.

page.name: product
page.description: The catalogue. One live list key feeds both the rows and the counts: search (fuzzy ladder, 250 ms debounce), kind/stock/margin/publish (Terbit, Belum terbit, Semua) filters, name/price/capital/stock sort with an "auto" relevance sort while searching, table or card view, and pagination — all in the URL (useListState) so a link reopens the same view; the view alone is also mirrored to the config service's `product-view` preference, so a bare `/products` reopens on the last layout. Admins get the floating add button. Rows gate on the key; the toolbar and footer are static.

subpages.subpage: The product form: info, one or more listings (code, price, unit, kind), alternative names, properties, images, initial stock lots.

Detail with three sub-tabs: Info (info/listings/properties/stock lots and the event journal), Image (gallery, drag-order, cover, delete), Performance (sales, margin and stock events over a range, lazy-loaded).

page.name: records
page.description: The day's history over the record service, read one local day at a time (useTime) and narrowed by a `query` matched in SQL. Two panes: the day's records on the left, the selected record on the right. Refetches keep the previous day on screen and fade it instead of blanking. Modes: Masuk (sale: money in, stock consumed) and Keluar (purchase: money out, stock received); the sort column/direction is in the URL (useOrder).

subpages.subpage: Comprehensive search across listing lines by name, mode and date range, with a capped page and the total match count.

One record in full, with Detail | Resi tabs in the URL. Detail shows the ledger (identity band, goods, charges, parties, totals, methods, images) and, admin only, the shelf actions: edit note, move the date, change mode, edit split payments, toggle credit, delete. Resi is the receipt it prints (lazy pdf-lib).

page.note: The record list does not filter RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT yet, so a dual charge's extras-only twin shows as a goods-less outcoming row — see <open_questions>.

page.name: money
page.description: Pockets ("kantong") over the money service. A draggable grid of cards (name, relative time, latest balance) — dragging persists the order through set.ordering — plus the Kantong Baru dialog. The page redirects non-admins itself because the alt+4 shortcut is not role-gated.

subpages.subpage: One pocket's ledger over a date range in the URL: editable name and type, the entries table (day, date, time, diff for `change` pockets, value, note), expandable rows, a settings dialog with delete-pocket / JSON upload / JSON download, and the new-entry button.

page.name: extra
page.description: The surcharge catalog: a fuzzy search box over a table of name, kind (Angka/Persen) and value, each row linking into its detail. Admins get a create button and the edit form (name, value, kind, and the dual flag); other roles see a read-only panel.

subpages.subpage: Detail: edit form for admins (with delete), read-only info panel for users.

page.name: debt
page.description: Outstanding customer credit over record.get.debt(): every credit record, since paying one clears it. A summary card totals the rows with decimal arithmetic and a sortable table lists date, note, total and a link into the record; the sort is in the URL (useSort). Re-reads on the record revision, so settling or deleting a record updates it.

page.name: cashier
page.description: The cashier roster over the cashier service: name, role, add, rename, re-role and delete. A new account is created as a `user` with an empty password; the cashier sets their own from Setting → Profile. Static head and add button; the list is the only key.

page.name: customer
page.description: The customer list over the customer service: name and phone, inline edit, add, soft delete. Static head; only the rows wait.

page.name: method
page.description: Payment methods over the method service. Tabs are the defaultable kinds (Transfer, Debit, QRIS) in the URL (useMethod); each tab lists the kind's named accounts plus its base method, with add, rename, set-as-default and soft delete. Static head and tabs; the catalog is the only key.

page.name: social
page.description: Receipt contact lines over the social service: name and value, add, edit, soft delete. Ordered by id so an edit never reshuffles the receipt.

page.name: analytics
page.description: A rail of five questions over one period. The period and bucket width live in the URL (useRange: presets 7/30/90 days, this month, this year; a hand-picked range clears the preset) and in the header, so switching pages never resets what you were looking at. The bodies are the lazy chart chunk; the rail and range bar are static.

subpages.subpage: Arus Kas (Cashflow): money in vs out per bucket, with totals.
Laba (Profit): margin over the period, from lines that stored a cost; days with no cost data say so.
Products: per-product qty/revenue/margin, sortable and paginated, expandable to the individual lines.
Time: sales per weekday and per hour, one week at a time.
Payments: what was tendered per method kind, plus the unpaid part of the period.

page.name: setting
page.description: One nav source (util-nav.ts) drives the index card grid and the sidebar, including which roles may open each destination; each screen's header quotes that row verbatim.

subpages.subpage: Signed-in account: rename (cashier.set.name + auth.set) and change password (Rust hash, then cashier.set.password).

Shop identity (owner, address, header, footer) through info, plus the show-cashier toggle; every field label and the save button are static and only the values pulse. The form patches the current info instead of overwriting it.
JSON export (Rust export_file) and import for products and records, with the skipped-row panel and a derived success/warning/error toast (describeUpload).
The log tail (bounded, newest first, warnings included) and a clear action, over the log service.
Printer picker, paper width in mm (Lebar Struk) and a test print, over the printer service and the Rust printer commands. The width decides how the receipt PDF is laid out.

page.name: dev_page_data
page.description: The page-data playground: a demo page with fast/slow/flaky keys, the Gate variants, stale and refreshing states, and the monitor that shows each key's status. It is also the place the legacy Result-based Gate still appears, labelled as such.

page.name: dev_page_cache
page.description: The page-cache inspector: entries by tag+deps, their kind, age, hits, stale/error state, plus clear/invalidate controls and the stats.

utilities.module: Money arithmetic for carts and records: lineSubtotal, lineGrandTotal, lineDiscountTotal, discountsEatLine, recalcDiscounts (clamped, order-dependent stack), withDerivedDiscounts, linesSubtotal, recalcExtras, extrasTotal, purchaseTotal, transactionGrandTotal, paidTotal, roundMoney. Decimal throughout.

module.name: lib/constants.ts
module.entry: App version, kept in step with package.json, Cargo.toml, tauri.conf.json and specification.xml.
["cash", "qris", "transfer", "debit"] — the order the Ctrl+0..3 keys follow.
Display names, key hints, key → kind, and the four built-in ids (1000 cash, 1003 qris, 1001 transfer, 1002 debit).
0b1 — the "books twice" bit of an extra's flag.
250 ms for search filters, 100 ms for cart writes.
The runtime time zone, used by every date-range bound and every date format.

utilities.module: formatDate / formatTime / getDayName / monthNames / MONTHS, and the picker bridge plainFromEpoch / epochFromPlain — all in the shop's zone, built on Temporal.

cn (tailwind-merge with the app's text-size tokens declared), numerish/numeric/integer (Zod string-number schemas that actually reject), urlBackOf/getURLBack (one parse for `?url_back=`: rooted, non-protocol-relative), capitalize (total on padded/empty names), formatError.
NotFound, InvokeError, InvalidCredential, IOError/ArrayBufferError/JsonError, TooBigError, DuplicateError. RedirectError was removed with the redirect loaders.
The two Tauri bcrypt bridges plus Unauthenticated. The session lives in the auth service.
saveJson(defaultName, value): serialise, then ask Rust (export_file) where to write. Cancelling is null, a failure is an IOError with the cashier sentence.
Product-image files under AppData/images: save (mkdir on first use), load → object URL, del. The key is the image_name, never the row id.
The Rust printer bridges: getPrinters and printPdf (which returns the spooler's sentence).
Fire-and-forget logging through plugin-log; a missing plugin or a rejected write never breaks the caller.
generateId() — a ULID for every row the app creates.
EARLIEST_EPOCH/FURTHEST_EPOCH and parseRange: URL epoch bounds that are safe for Temporal and fall back per bound.
describeUpload + notifyUpload: the one success/warning/error sentence for the three import panels.
canRead/writeText/readText: the async clipboard first, an execCommand("copy") fallback for the webview, and an honest "cannot read" for the paste-key path.

normalize (casefold/accents/punctuation, compact), quality (the match ladder and code grading), index-cache (the signature-gated index, parseQuery, toHit, sortHits), listings (the restock catalogue index).

The PDF pipeline: create-receipt-data orchestrates; build-header (shop, datetime, cashier), product-text-data (lines, discounts), build-summary (totals, extras, rounding, pay, change), build-transaction-summary (species/pieces and the split payments), extras-text-data, build-footer (footer lines + contacts); index.ts lays out and saves the PDF (pdf-lib + Roboto via ?arraybuffer, wrapped by splitWrappedText).

module.name: hooks/
module.hook: The signed-in user from the auth service; throws Unauthenticated when there is none.
The UI size from the config service.
Today's local midnight, re-armed at the next midnight and on focus/visibilitychange.
The "a dialog owns the keyboard" counter + aria-modal fallback, read by every window listener.
Memoised microfuzz over any { name } row.
Resolves a stored image to an object URL; revokes on unmount and on a late load.
Keep an incoming `url_back` / build a back-link from the current base and query.

feature.name: sync_rebuild
feature.description: Build a sync service over the current schema (soft `_deleted_at`, nested product/record payloads, per-entity unsync reads) and restore the Sinkronisasi screen and floating status pill designed in <sync_ui_design>. The server contract is in backend-docs/openapi.yaml.

feature.name: record_list_flag_filter
feature.description: Filter RECORD_FLAG_ADJUSTMENT out of the /records list (or show the twin differently). Noted as the open piece in FLAGS.md: a dual charge's extras-only twin currently shows as a goods-less outcoming row.

feature.name: analytics_server_side
feature.description: Analytics currently reads every record in the range and aggregates in SQL per question. If a shop's history outgrows that, the aggregates move behind materialised per-day tables.

feature.name: product_event_batching
feature.description: When sync is rebuilt: split product-event pull into batches so a shop with many products does not send one oversized list of ids.

item.name: setting_printer_guard
item.description: Setting printer has no role guard: the sidebar and util-nav mark it admin-only, but the route renders for any signed-in user. Either wrap it in AdminOnly or change the nav metadata.

item.name: dual_twin_row
item.description: Decide how a dual charge's extras-only twin should read in /records: two rows, one row with a badge, or the twin hidden. It is deliberately visible until that decision, so the list keeps showing what the table actually holds.

item.name: leftover_tables
item.description: Migrations 43/44 park every replaced table as `<name>_old` rather than dropping it (records_old, products_old, graves_old, …). They are never read; a follow-up migration could drop them, but only after every installed database has been through 44.

item.name: vanilla_extract
item.description: @vanilla-extract/vite-plugin is still configured although no `.css.ts` source exists. Either drop the dependency/plugin or start using it; today all styling is Tailwind + global.css tokens.
